title: Shoulder, Neck, Trap & Scalene Pain, Mobility & Decompression Protocol
tagline: 6-Week Progressive Release, Eccentric & Rotator Cuff Control System

principles.title: The #1 Rule — Shoulders live in your pockets
Incorrect
principles.text: Shoulders pulled up. Traps tight. Neck looks short. Leads to pain and tension.

principles.title: Correct
principles.text: Shoulders down. Elbows toward pockets. Neck long and relaxed. Traps quiet.

weeks.label: Week 1 of 6
weeks.focus: Phase 1: Decompression, Exploratory Range & Awareness. Calm the nervous system → Establish the shoulder-down pattern → Release what is guarding
weeks.notes:
Better posture. Less pain. A stronger you.

HOW TO DO IT:
- Actively pull your shoulders downward — not backward.
- Think: elbows and shoulders sliding into your front pockets.
- Keep your neck long and relaxed.
- Let your traps stay quiet.
- Breathe naturally.
- This position should feel light and easy, not forced.
KEY CUE: "My shoulders live in my pockets."

USE THIS POSITION DURING:
- Walking
- Sitting
- Desk work
- Driving
- Holding a phone
- Opening doors
- Exercising
DO NOT:
- Pull the shoulders back
- Pinch the shoulder blades together
- Stand in "military posture"
This rule continues permanently — even after the protocol ends.

WEEK 1 OBJECTIVE: The goal is not to eliminate every symptom in seven days. Week 1 teaches the body three critical things:
- Create awareness and stop the habit of shoulder hiking.
- Release what is guarding (scalenes).
- Begin to lengthen under control (eccentric shrug drop).
- Build the shoulder-down position into daily life.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTICE:
Scalene release work can be painful. It is common to feel pain that:
- Radiates into the head
- Travels down the arm
- Refers into the chest or upper back
STOP IMMEDIATELY if you experience:
- Dizziness
- Visual changes
- Persistent numbness or tingling
- Loss of strength

WHAT'S NOT INCLUDED YET:
- No rotator cuff internal/external rotation (save for later).
- No end-range holds.
- No chin rotation during scalene release.
- No rotator cuff work in abduction.
- No farmer carries (start in Week 2).
- No cable pulldowns.
- No bear crawls.
- This week is about awareness, decompression, and building the foundation.

Consistent habits create lasting change.
Small steps today. A stronger, pain-free tomorrow.

exercises.name: Scalene Release (Both Sides)
exercises.whenToUse: Decompress and calm the nervous system
howTo: Sit in a chair with good posture.
Drop the affected shoulder downward (inverse shrug).
Gently tilt the ear toward the same-side shoulder — no rotation.
Apply firm thumb pressure to the exposed muscle ridge at the lateral edge of the neck (scalene area).
Breathe slowly and allow the muscle to soften.
Repeat on the opposite side.
focus: Pain and referred symptoms into the head, shoulder, chest, upper back or arm are normal.

exercises.name: Eccentric Dumbbell Shrug Drop
howTo: Use both hands to help pre-raise the dumbbell (15-25 lb).
Transfer the weight to the affected side.
Keep the shoulder down and relaxed.
Slowly lower the shoulder (eccentric) — 3-5 seconds.
At the bottom, gently push the dumbbell toward the floor for a deeper stretch.
exercises.proTip: KEY CUE: "Don't shrug the weight up. Control it DOWN."

exercises.name: Daily Awareness & Reminders
howTo: Set a phone alarm every 1-2 hours.
Use a custom reminder like "Shoulders Down."
Pair it with a deep breath and quick posture check.
Do this every day — at work, at home, and while driving.
Consistency rewires posture and reduces pain.
focus: Are my shoulders down?
Is my neck long and relaxed?
Are my traps quiet?
Am I breathing normally?

weeks.label: Week 2 of 6
weeks.focus: Phase 1: Decompression, Exploratory Range & Initial Cuff Control. Build consistency → Add the farmer carry → Continue → 6calbne scalene release → Intro gentle movement tolerance
weeks.notes:
Discipline builds freedom. Better shoulders. A brighter you.

DAILY FOCUS THIS WEEK:
- Maintain shoulder-down posture all day.
- Continue scalene release (both sides).
- Perform eccentric shrug drops.
- Add farmer carries.
- Stay consistent with phone reminders.
- Move more with good posture.
- Build tolerance without forcing it.
KEY CUE: "My shoulders live in my pockets."

SET YOUR REMINDERS:
- Set a phone alarm every 1-2 hours.
- Use a custom reminder: "Shoulders Down."
- Pair it with a deep breath and quick posture check.
- Use visual cues at your desk, car, and home.
- Consistency rewires posture and reduces pain.
"Small, frequent reminders create big, lasting changes."

WEEK 2 OBJECTIVE: Build on Week 1 by adding movement while maintaining the shoulder-down posture.
- Keep shoulders down throughout the day.
- Continue scalene release (both sides).
- Perform eccentric shrug drops.
- Add farmer carries.
- Develop consistency with reminders.
- Reduce daily tension and improve tolerance.

PROGRESSIONS FROM WEEK 1:
- Continue everything from Week 1.
- Add farmer carries.
- Slightly increase dumbbell weight if tolerated (15-25 lb).
- Improve posture awareness during daily activities.
- Build confidence with the shoulder-down position.
- More consistent breathing and movement breaks.

IMPORTANT SAFETY NOTICE:
Scalene release work can be painful. It is common to feel pain that:
- Radiates into the head
- Travels down the arm
- Refers into the chest or upper back
STOP IMMEDIATELY if you experience:
- Dizziness
- Visual changes
- Persistent numbness or tingling
- Loss of strength

WHAT'S NEXT (WEEKS 3-4):
- Add chin rotation at end range.
- Add 3-5 second holds.
- Increase band resistance for rotator cuff work.
- Integrate more cervical control.
- Progress farmer carry load.
- Continue daily posture and breathing work.

Consistent habits. Real results.
Small steps today. A stronger tomorrow.

exercises.whenToUse: Teach the shoulders to stay down while moving

exercises.name: Breathing Reset
howTo: Sit or stand with shoulders down.
Inhale slowly through the nose for 4 seconds.
Exhale slowly through the nose or mouth for 6 seconds.
Feel the shoulders relax downward on the exhale.
Repeat for 1-2 minutes, 3-5× daily.
focus: Better breathing supports lower muscle tension and less pain.

exercises.name: Desk Setup & Posture Check
howTo: Screen at eye level.
Feet flat on the floor.
Hips slightly higher than knees.
Elbows close to your side.
Shoulders down and relaxed.
Set recurring reminders.
Take short movement breaks every hour.

- Chin rotation at bottom of shrug drops.

howTo: Drop the affected shoulder (inverse shrug).

exercises.name: Eccentric Dumbbell Shrug Drop

Slowly lower the shoulder (eccentric) — 3-5 seconds.

exercises.name: Rotator Cuff Internal / External Rotation
howTo: Elbow bent ~90° and pinned to ribs.
Actively push elbow toward the floor.
Keep the shoulder down and relaxed.
Rotate outward to light tightness and hold 3-5 seconds.
Rotate inward toward belly button and hold 3-5 seconds.
Elbow never leaves ribs.
exercises.proTip: KEY CUE: "My elbow is heavy. My arm rotates inside the socket."

howTo: Dumbbells: 15-25 lb each (start light, increase gradually).
Stand tall, long neck, quiet traps.
Push the weights toward the floor.
Walk 20-30 ft per lap.
focus: Focus on quality posture, not speed or heavy weight.

howTo: Pull shoulder and elbow downward as if into your front pocket.
Tilt the ear toward the shoulder.
Hold 3-5 seconds.
Repeat throughout the day whenever remembered.
focus: This reinforces the shoulder-down position between exercise sessions.

exercises.name: Scalene Stretch — Three Part
howTo: Drop the affected shoulder downward.
Tilt ear toward opposite shoulder.
Slowly rotate chin away (end range).
Gently tuck the chin.
Hold each position 3-5 seconds.
Breathe slowly and allow the muscle to soften.
Repeat on the other side.
focus: You should feel a stretch without sharp pain. Mild referred symptoms are normal.

exercises.name: Eccentric + Concentric Dumbbell Shrug
exercises.whenToUse: Lengthen then strengthen at new length
howTo: Use both hands to help pre-raise the dumbbell (15-25 lb).
Transfer the weight to the affected side.
Slowly lower the shoulder (eccentric) — 3-5 seconds.
At the bottom, pause and gently push the weight toward the floor.
Now actively squeeze the shoulder up (concentric) — 1-2 seconds.
Keep neck long, shoulder down, and head neutral.
exercises.proTip: KEY CUE: "Lengthen down. Squeeze up. Stronger at the new length."

exercises.name: Rotator Cuff Rotation in Abduction
howTo: Arm abducted as if waving, elbow ~90°.
Shoulder stays down — not back.
Rotate fist backward (external) to light tightness.
Rotate fist forward/down (internal) on same axis.
Keep elbow stable and controlled.
Hold 3-5 seconds at each end range.
Use a light band — increase resistance as tolerated.
exercises.proTip: KEY CUE: "Shoulder stays down. Rotate, don't shrug."

exercises.name: Kneeling Straight-Arm Cable Pulldown
howTo: Kneel facing cable (or use band).
Arms straight, slight forward lean.
Pull hands down toward thighs.
Keep shoulders down and core engaged.
Pause 1-2 seconds at the bottom.
Control the return.
exercises.proTip: KEY CUE: "Arms long. Shoulders down. Engage the lats."

exercises.name: Bear Crawls
howTo: Hands under shoulders, knees low (off or near floor).
Keep knees and toes wide.
Move slowly and with control (20-30 ft).
Maintain a flat back and engaged core.
Keep shoulders down and away from ears.
exercises.proTip: KEY CUE: "Move with control. Shoulders down. Core on."

exercises.name: Daily Posture & Breathing Integration
howTo: Head level
Chin slightly tucked
Shoulders down
Ribs over pelvis
Glutes lightly engaged
Breathe through your nose
focus: This position should feel natural, not forced.
Small, frequent posture checks create lasting change.

other.Use throughout the dax: Desk work; Walking; Driving; Phone use; At home

- Perform eccentric + concentric shrug drops.
- Rotator cuff rotation in abduction.

- Bear crawls.
- Use the shoulder-down position in all daily activities.
- Build long-term resilience.
- Keep the gains beyond 6 weeks.

LONG-TERM SUCCESS:

- Maintain shoulder-down posture for life.

From the PDF:
Title: SHOULDER, NECK, TRAP & SCALENE PAIN, MOBILITY & DECOMPRESSION PROTOCOL / 6-Week Progressive Release, Eccentric & Rotator Cuff Control System
⚠ MOST IMPORTANT RULE — READ FIRST THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT PART OF THIS ENTIRE PROTOCOL. IF THIS RULE IS NOT FOLLOWED CONSISTENTLY, THE REST OF THE PROGRAM WILL NOT HOLD AND PAIN WILL RETURN. SHOULDERS MUST LIVE IN YOUR POCKETS — ALL DAY, EVERY DAY, LIGHTLY PULLED DOWN. At all times throughout the day, your shoulders must be actively pulled DOWNWARD — NOT BACKWARD. Think: Elbows and shoulders sliding into your front pockets Heavy shoulders Long, relaxed neck Quiet traps ... This rule applies during: Walking Sitting Standing Opening doors Desk work Holding a phone Driving Exercising
PROGRAM INTENT: This protocol reduces pain and restores mobility in the shoulder, neck, chest, and arm by addressing: Scalenes (anterior, middle, posterior) Upper trapezius Rotator cuff Deltoid Cervicothoracic mechanics. This system prioritizes: Soft-tissue decompression Eccentric length under load Elbow-driven rotator cuff control Cervical positioning Progressive integration into movement. This is not stretching and not strength training. This is controlled exposure and tolerance restoration.
PHASE 1 — WEEKS 1–2 DECOMPRESSION, EXPLORATORY RANGE & INITIAL CUFF CONTROL
1. Scalene Release (Self or Assisted): Drop the affected shoulder downward (inverse shrug). Actively squeeze the lat on that side. Tilt the head away from the affected shoulder. Apply firm thumb pressure to the exposed muscle ridge at the lateral edge of the upper trapezius. Dosage: 30–60 seconds 1–2 rounds. Pain and referred symptoms are normal.
2. Eccentric Dumbbell Shrug Drop: Dumbbell: 15–25 lb. Pre-raise shoulder using both hands. Transfer weight to affected side. Tilt head away. Slowly lower shoulder. At bottom, gently push dumbbell toward the floor. Dosage: 10–20 reps Up to 2× daily
3. Rotator Cuff Internal / External Rotation (At Side): Positioning: Elbow bent ~90° Elbow pinned firmly against ribs Actively push elbow toward the floor Shoulder stays down and relaxed. Movement: Rotate fist outward to light tightness Rotate inward toward belly button Elbow never leaves ribs. Dosage: 15–20 reps 1–2 sets Very light band or no resistance. Mental cue: “My elbow is heavy. My arm rotates inside the socket.”
4. Repeated Shoulder Drop Stretch (Daily Habit): Pull elbow and shoulder downward as if into front pocket Tilt head away Hold 3–5 seconds. Frequency: As often as remembered throughout the day
5. Farmer Carries: Dumbbells: 15–20 lb each Stand tall Push weights toward the floor Walk 20–30 ft per lap. Dosage: 10–20 laps
PHASE 2 — WEEKS 3–4 END-RANGE CONTROL & CERVICAL ROTATION: Add chin rotation at end range for scalene stretches Add chin rotation at bottom of shrug drops Slightly increase band resistance Add 3–5 second holds at both ends of rotator cuff rotation Gradually increase farmer carry load
PHASE 3 — WEEKS 5–6 FULL CERVICAL CONTROL & GLOBAL INTEGRATION: Scalene Stretch — Three-Part Sequence Each repetition: Head tilt Chin rotation Chin tuck Hold each position 3–5 seconds. Rotator Cuff Rotation in Abduction: Arm abducted as if waving Elbow ~90° Shoulder stays down, not back Rotate fist downward/forward to light pull Rotate backward on same axis. Dosage: 10–15 reps 2 sets. Add: Kneeling straight-arm cable pulldowns (3 × 12–20 reps) Bear crawls (20–30 ft, 4–6 sets)
SUCCESS MARKERS: Reduced neck and shoulder pain Decreased referred pain Improved overhead comfort Improved postural endurance Reduced reliance on release work
FINAL STATEMENT: “The releases calm the tissue. The movements restore control. The daily shoulder-down posture keeps the pain from coming back.”
